content.content: Recent articles discuss surface code threshold demonstrations and real-time decoding bottlenecks.

result: Quantum error correction protects fragile qubit states by spreading one logical qubit across many physical qubits so that local noise can be detected and undone. The leading approach in 2026 is the surface code, and several groups have now pushed below the fault-tolerance threshold, meaning that adding more physical qubits lowers the logical error rate. The biggest remaining obstacle is building classical decoding hardware fast enough to keep up with the error stream in real time.
